  "..........K",

  "...........",
  "...........",
  "...........",
  "L..........",
  ".........L.",
  "......L....",
  "...........",
];

// y 21: the lamps on the desk and the table, and a flower pot on the desk

  "....L.A....",
  "...........",
  "...........",
  "...........",
  "...........",

export function build(g) {
  layers(g, [26, 19, 9], LEGEND, [FLOOR, TOP, LAMPS]);
}

input.summary:
parts/room-4.mjs (H1 loft) now builds with 0 refused writes and 0 off-palette blocks; make.sh produces build.nbt.
Fix: removed the 9 y 20 writes that landed on the roof's eave stairs (bookshelves at x 26/36 z 11..16, one lantern at 26,20,20); y 19 furniture and the desk/table are unchanged.
Palette was already clean, so the off-palette swap was a no-op.
left: The H1 loft lost its top shelves on the west and east eave edges (x 26 and x 36, z 11..16) and the lantern at 26,20,20. The y 19 bookshelves there remain. Re-seating those shelves against the slope needs a design call, not a fix.
make.sh's REFUSED line reported 9 but listed only 8 cells; the ninth (the lantern at 26,20,20) was only visible in parts-report.json. Not a room-4 problem, but the summary line under-reports.

waste.what: Found the refused cells by matching each refused coordinate back to a row and column of the TOP grid by hand (x = 26 + column, z = 9 + row), then worked out which rows to blank.
waste.cost: About 8 cells checked by hand over one pass, plus one extra make.sh run to catch the lantern the first listing hid.
waste.tool: A `mcd plan`-style pre-check (or a dry-run mode for layers()) that prints the layer grid with occupied cells marked from earlier parts, so refusals show as cell marks before make.sh. The refusal lines should print all refused cells, not a truncated sample.

waste.what: Built the one-cell replacements by hand, rewriting rows of the ASCII grid.
waste.cost: Two Edit calls and two make.sh runs (about 60 s each).
waste.tool: layers() could take an option such as { skipOccupied: true } that drops occupied cells and logs them, which would have made this fix automatic. The part's author would still need to decide whether to re-seat the shelves.

companions.task: Redesign the H1 loft's west and east shelving so the y 20 bookshelves fit the roof's eave slope, instead of the cells being blanked out. Hand over the y 19 and y 20 cell maps and the eave stair positions.
